_about: Village square. Lines are [speaker, text]. Speakers live in data/speakers.json. Format reference: scripts/autoload/dialogue_manager.gd
pip_intro: No. But everyone who comes back to this village is late for something.
I'm ten. I'm allowed to be strange.
You hear it too, don't you?
Grandma used to sing that. Except nobody remembers Grandma singing.

choice.text: Then how do you know she did?

pip_intro: It is, isn't it? Nobody else thinks so. Nobody else even hears it.
Because I remember. I'm the only one who does. That's the strange part, not me.
At the tower, maybe. He went up yesterday.
He said if the bell stopped, we shouldn't be afraid of what comes out of the mist.
Then what should we be afraid of?
Before he went up, he was at the forge, shouting at Mara about iron and tuning and... I stopped listening.
Mara's on the west side of the square. Follow the smoke. And the swearing.
pip: Mara's forge is on the west side. Follow the smoke. And the swearing.
Did Mara yell at you? She yells at everybody. It means she likes you. Or that you're standing too close to the anvil.
Is that the bell's pin? Can I hold it?
It's cold. Colder than iron should be. Like it's been somewhere.
Fine. I didn't want to anyway.
Brother Alden says the chapel keeps everything worth keeping. Maybe it keeps whatever that pin is for.
The chapel's east of the square. Alden's the one who looks like a worried candle.
You look like you've been reading. You get a face. Grandma got the same face.
I'll keep humming it. Somebody should.

pip.text: Bring Orin home, if you can. Or bring home whatever's left of him.

pip_song: The song you hum. Your grandmother's. Can you hum it once more? Slowly?
Because I think I've seen it written down.
Wait. I know how it ends.{p} I don't know how I know.
You look like you've seen a ghost.
I knew it. I always know.
Better? Huh. Nobody's used that word around here in ages.
It isn't a lullaby. It's a calling. Everyone sang it together, once. Before there was a bell.
Everyone? Even Mara? She can't sing. I've heard her try.
...Then I'll teach her. If you think it matters.
I think it might be the only thing that does.
tobin: Evening. Or is it? I lit this one already, didn't I. Or I meant to.
Tobin. Thirty years on the lanterns. You'd think I'd remember which ones I've done.
I keep lighting the one by the well, though. Twice a night, sometimes. Never knew why.

tobin.text: You're going up the tower road? Take a lantern. Take two. Take mine, if you're daft enough to need it.
Mind the mist by the gate. It's been leaning on the wall all evening, like it's waiting to be let in.

tobin: Tobin. Does the name Elsie mean anything to you?
...No. No, I don't know an Elsie.
Funny. My hands went cold just now.
Well. The one by the well won't light itself.
Habit, that lantern. Just habit. Good night to you.
cat: The cat regards you with deep suspicion, then permits exactly one scratch behind the ear.
The cat leans into your hand. It has decided you are furniture, which is a kind of trust.
The cat purrs like a small, warm engine. Whatever the bell takes, it hasn't taken this.
village_well: Someone carved two names into the stone.
The first says TOBIN. The second has been worn away, like something kept rubbing at it.

village_well.text: The stone feels colder than it should. Some places remember more than they show. (Stand close and press F to listen.)

village_well: TOBIN, and ELSIE. Hard to see. Easy to know, once you've heard it.
village_well_echo: [wave amp=12 freq=3]You promised you'd wait for me.[/wave]
TOBIN... and ELSIE. The second name came back, just for a moment.
Somebody made a promise here. Somebody else forgot it.
village_signpost: WEST: the forge. EAST: the chapel. NORTH: the tower road.
Someone has carved a fourth arm, pointing at nothing. It just says: HOME?
village_stall: A fruit stall, abandoned mid-sale. A sign leans against the apples: BACK BEFORE THE BELL.
village_gate: The north gate is chained shut. The lock is stamped with a small bell.
Beyond the bars, the tower road disappears into mist.

village_gate.text: Orin would have had a key. Orin had a key for everything.

village_gate: A bell on the lock. A bell on the key. Of course.
The chain slides free. The gate swings inward, and the mist leans in to meet you.
village_door_nw: You knock. From inside, a muffled voice: “We're not buying any!”
village_door_ne: Shutters drawn. Someone inside is humming, badly, and stops the moment you knock.
village_door_sw: A note is pinned to the door: OUT. Under it, in older ink: IN. Under that, older still: WHO?
village_tavern: The Lantern and Last Orders. Closed. A sign hangs on the door:
GONE TO BED EARLY. BELL'S BROKEN. DON'T ASK.
village_cart: A cart packed for a journey nobody took. The apples on top have started to wrinkle.
village_leave: Not yet. Orin's letter brought me home for a reason.
If I turn back now, the mist gets the village. I didn't walk all this way for that.
